 The Scot: it happened before his debut against Haiti
 11 November 2026 at 11:15 
 1 min read 
 Napoli: McTominay reflects on the heart problems that emerged during the World Cup: “Before the opening match against Haiti, I needed a shock to my heart. I’m fine now.”
 A difficult period is finally behind him. Scott McTominay spoke about the heart problems that emerged during the World Cup, which were subsequently resolved by surgical ablation – which he underwent on 8 September – to correct the benign arrhythmia.
 The Napoli star looked back on what happened before Scotland’s match against Haiti: “There were two days to go,” he said, “and I was in excellent shape. Then I needed a defibrillator shock to my heart. I found myself in a hospital bed, about to be put to sleep under anaesthetic. I thought, ‘Is this really happening to me?’”
 The Napoli star has found the strength to move on: “You have to keep going.” McTominay was sidelined again after the match against Como and underwent surgery to resolve the issue once and for all: “I’m fine now. It was something that had to be done. In a footballer’s career, there can be moments when events catch you off guard, but you bounce back. The reports on TV and in the newspapers alarmed my friends and family a bit, but the operation I had in Manchester was fairly straightforward. I’m feeling really well now and I’m happy to be back playing. Football is the most important part of my life. I always want to prove my worth and make sure I can reach an even higher level. The goal is to be stronger than before.”
 McTominay has been recalled to the national team after missing Scotland’s Nations League fixtures in September and October: he will face North Macedonia on Friday and Switzerland away on Monday.
